name: screen.capture
description: Pixel capture of region, window, monitor, or virtual screen. If neither region nor window nor monitor is supplied, the entire virtual screen is captured. Returned bytes are base64-encoded image data by default; pass `encoding: binary` for raw bytes.

region.description: Rectangle in virtual-screen coordinates. Mutually exclusive with `window` and `monitor`.

window.description: Window handle, e.g. 'win:0x1A2B'. Mutually exclusive with `region` and `monitor`.

monitor.description: Zero-based monitor index as reported by `system.info.screens`. Mutually exclusive with `region` and `window`.

format.description: Output image format. Family-dependent — `system.info.capabilities.image_formats` reports what the connected agent actually supports (composed from each x-implementations entry's `produces_formats`). Requesting an unsupported format returns ERR unsupported_format. `jpeg` and `heic` are forward-compat enum entries reserved for future families (macOS, Linux); current Windows families (`windows-modern`, `windows-legacy`, `windows-classic`) emit `ERR unsupported_format` for those values.

quality.description: Encoder quality, 1-100. Only meaningful for lossy formats (`webp`, `jpeg`, `heic`); silently ignored for `png`/`bmp`. Optional — when omitted, agents use their encoder-appropriate default (libwebp, WIC, GDI+ each carry their own sensible default; no spec-mandated value). See issue #83.

cursor.description: Composite the OS cursor into the captured image at its current position. Default true (operator click-target visibility). Hidden / off-region cursors no-op gracefully. See issue #66.

encoding.description: Response payload encoding. `base64` (default) is JSON-safe / transport-friendly. `binary` is raw image bytes — 33% smaller, requires binary-aware client framing. See issue #91.

x-output-schema.description: Image bytes. Base64-encoded by default (matches `format: byte`); raw binary when `encoding: binary` is supplied.

x-implementations.name: wgc
x-implementations.description: Windows.Graphics.Capture (WGC) fast path. Win 10 1809+ (build 17763); WGC API was introduced in 1803 but unstable until 1809. Composes via DWM — captures DirectComposition / hardware-accelerated content correctly. WIC-backed encoder produces PNG/WebP/BMP.

x-implementations.name: gdi_bitblt
x-implementations.description: Win32 `BitBlt` from the desktop DC. Universal fallback — emits raw BMP; PNG/WebP encoding requires WIC (modern) or GDI+ (classic, see `gdi_plus`). Misses hardware cursor unless `cursor: true` (which composites separately via DrawIcon).

x-implementations.name: print_window
x-implementations.description: Win32 `PrintWindow` for window-specific captures. Used when `window` is supplied; reaches some occluded/minimized windows BitBlt cannot. Same BMP-only emit as gdi_bitblt; encoding to PNG/WebP layered on top.

x-implementations.name: gdi_plus
x-implementations.description: GDI+ runtime encoder for PNG output on classic. NT 4 SP6+ requires the GDI+ redistributable; XP+ ships GDI+ in the box. Layered on top of gdi_bitblt's raw BMP buffer.

windows-modern.description: WGC fast path on Win 10 1809+ (build 17763); WGC API introduced 1803, stable from 1809. GDI BitBlt fallback if WGC is unavailable on a particular session (e.g. cross-IL or DRM-protected content). PNG/WebP/BMP via WIC. Multi-monitor full. Cursor overlay via GetCursorInfo + DrawIcon when `cursor: true`.

windows-classic.description: GDI BitBlt only for the desktop / region path; PrintWindow when `window` is supplied. BMP always; PNG via GDI+ when the runtime is detected (NT 4 SP6+ with redist; XP+ ships GDI+). Multi-monitor: NT 4 single-display, 2000+ multi. Cursor overlay via GetCursorInfo + DrawIcon when `cursor: true`.
